shots.subject: The regents meet beside Hideyoshi's empty seat
shots.prompt:
Interior of a great hall at Fushimi Castle, autumn 1598, night, rain outside.
In the centre, an empty raised cushion before a gilded folding screen of pine
trees: the seat of the late ruler Hideyoshi. Five senior lords in formal dark
robes and court hats sit facing one another in two tense rows on the tatami,
lit by tall paper lanterns. One older lord with a grey beard (Tokugawa Ieyasu)
sits a little apart, watching the others. Long shadows, polished wet-looking
wooden floor, rain visible through open shutters.
shots.history: Hideyoshi died at Fushimi in September 1598. The regents are civil, not armored, in this scene.
shots.accept: Empty seat is the clear focal point; lords are in robes, not armor; no text on the screen.
shots.caption: Autumn 1598. Hideyoshi is dead, and the regents who swore to protect his young heir now watch one another.

shots.subject: Ieyasu's Edo: granaries, roads and workers
shots.prompt:
Edo in 1599 seen from a low hill on an overcast afternoon: a modest castle
town of wooden buildings and earthen walls beside marshy bay shores, NOT a
tall stone keep. In the foreground, rows of thatched storehouses with workers
carrying rice bales; ox carts on a muddy road leading away west; a few
Eastern navy banners with a white round crest. Light drizzle, low clouds,
smoke from cooking fires.
shots.history: Edo in 1599 was a growing but modest town; the great Edo keep came later (1607). Keep the castle low and simple.
shots.accept: Reads as a busy supply base; no grand white keep; navy Eastern banners.
shots.caption: At Edo, Ieyasu fills his granaries and repairs his roads. Every bale and bridge may matter when the promises break.

shots.subject: Ishida Mitsunari watching from Osaka
shots.prompt:
Osaka Castle at dusk: a tall dark keep with gold-trimmed roofs on massive
stone walls above a wide moat. On a high balcony, a lone armored figure with a
white feather plume on his helmet (Ishida Mitsunari) looks out toward the east,
seen from behind and slightly to the side. Crimson Western banners with a dark
round crest hang along the walls. Heavy clouds, last orange light on the
horizon, rain starting.
shots.history: Osaka was the seat of Hideyoshi's heir, Hideyori. Ishida led the faction opposed to Ieyasu.
shots.accept: Ishida's white plume readable; Osaka keep imposing; crimson banners.
shots.caption: From Osaka, Ishida Mitsunari gathers lords who fear Ieyasu's ambition.

shots.subject: Uesugi troops fortify Aizu in the northern mountains
shots.prompt:
Rugged, forested northern mountains in early summer 1600, mist in the
valleys. On a ridge, Uesugi soldiers dig earthworks and raise a wooden
palisade around a hilltop fort; others haul timber up a switchback path.
Their banners are crimson with a dark round crest (they oppose Ieyasu).
Green summer foliage, grey sky, light rain.
shots.history: Uesugi Kagekatsu's domain of Aizu; his fortification work was the pretext for Ieyasu's campaign. Season: early summer, not snow.
shots.accept: Summer greenery (no snow); fortification work visible; crimson banners.
shots.caption: Far to the north, Uesugi Kagekatsu fortifies Aizu. Ieyasu calls it defiance and prepares to march.

shots.subject: The Eastern army marches north out of Edo
shots.prompt:
A long column of Eastern troops leaves Edo along a raised road between
flooded rice paddies, summer 1600, early morning. Mounted samurai in dark
armor lead; behind them spearmen, arquebusiers with matchlocks on their
shoulders, pack horses with supplies. Many tall navy banners with a white
round crest. Mist over the paddies, a pale sun behind cloud.
shots.history: July 1600: Ieyasu's army marched north from Edo toward Oyama and Aizu.
shots.accept: Column reads as a large organized army; navy banners; summer paddies.
shots.caption: The army marches north toward Aizu. Every soldier on the road eats from Edo's granaries.

shots.subject: Edo left lightly guarded
shots.prompt:
Dusk at an Edo gate after the army has gone: a heavy wooden gate in an
earthen wall, only two old ashigaru guards with spears under a single navy
banner. The road beyond is empty and wet. Townspeople glance nervously
toward the west. Rain, lantern glow, long empty shadows.
shots.history: The march drew troops away from the Tokugawa home base.
shots.accept: Feeling of emptiness and vulnerability; very few defenders.
shots.caption: Behind the marching army, Edo's walls are thinly held.

shots.subject: A rider reaches the camp at Oyama
shots.prompt:
Night field camp at Oyama, late summer 1600: white curtain walls (maku)
with navy round crests, tall navy banners, campfires. A mud-spattered rider
on an exhausted horse gallops in from the left (the west), a small red
messenger flag on his back. Guards turn toward him; one raises a lantern.
Moonlight through drifting rain clouds.
shots.history: Oyama, in Shimotsuke, August 1600: Ieyasu learned that the West had risen. A field camp, not a castle.
shots.accept: Rider enters from the left; field camp with maku curtains; no castle keep.
shots.caption: Oyama, late summer 1600. Ieyasu's army is camped on the road north to Aizu when a rider comes in from the west.

shots.subject: Fushimi Castle burns
shots.prompt:
Fushimi Castle at night under siege: a multi-tiered castle keep on stone
walls is burning, flames and sparks rising into heavy smoke, the sky glowing
orange. Below the walls, a small group of Eastern defenders with navy
banners hold a gate against masses of attackers with crimson banners and
ladders. Embers drifting, rain hissing in the fire, dramatic low angle.
No gore.
shots.history: Torii Mototada held Fushimi with a small garrison for about ten days before it fell (September 1600).
shots.accept: Burning keep is the focal point; defenders clearly outnumbered; navy vs crimson; no gore.
shots.caption: The Western army has besieged Fushimi Castle. Its keeper, Torii Mototada, holds out for days to buy Ieyasu time. Then the castle falls.

shots.subject: The Oyama council: the lords choose to turn west
shots.prompt:
Inside a field-camp command enclosure (white maku curtains with navy round
crests), daylight filtered through cloud. Armored lords sit on folding
stools in a horseshoe around a map laid on the ground. Ieyasu (older, grey
beard, black helmet with gold round crest) sits at the centre. One lord with
a wide gold crescent on his black helmet (Fukushima Masanori) has risen to
his feet, fist raised, declaring his support. The others look to him.
shots.history: At the Oyama council (August 1600) Fukushima Masanori spoke first for marching west with Ieyasu.
shots.accept: Fukushima's gold crescent and standing pose clear; Ieyasu recognizable; outdoor enclosure, not a hall.
shots.caption: “My army marches west with Lord Ieyasu.” At Oyama, the allied lords decide to turn back and fight.

shots.subject: Gifu Castle falls to the Eastern vanguard
shots.prompt:
Gifu Castle on top of a steep forested mountain (Mount Kinka) above a river
plain, morning, broken cloud. Eastern troops with navy banners stream up the
mountain paths and over the outer walls; smoke rises from the gate; a navy
banner is being raised at the summit castle. The river and town below in
mist.
shots.history: Gifu stood on Mount Kinka; Eastern forces under Fukushima and Ikeda took it in late September 1600.
shots.accept: Castle clearly on a mountaintop; navy banners winning; smoke but no gore.
shots.caption: Your vanguard storms Gifu. The road into Mino lies open.

shots.subject: Gifu Castle still holds
shots.prompt:
The same mountaintop castle (Mount Kinka) above a river plain, seen from
the plain at dusk. Crimson Western banners still fly along its walls and
gate; Eastern scouts with navy banners watch from the reeds by the river,
too few to attack. Overcast, mist rising from the river.
shots.history: Alternative to CH4-P1A when the player did not secure Gifu.
shots.accept: Same castle design as CH4-P1A; crimson banners on the walls; Eastern scouts small and distant.
shots.caption: Gifu still flies Western banners. Your army must enter Mino by a narrower road.
shots.branch: Shown if Gifu was not secured.

shots.subject: Rain over the Mino plain; two armies' campfires
shots.prompt:
A wide valley in Mino on the night before battle, heavy rain. On the left,
hundreds of small campfires and navy banners of the Eastern army; on the
right, across a stream and low hills, the crimson banners and fires of the
Western army. Dark mountains close in on both sides. Puddles reflect the
firelight.
shots.history: The armies converged on Sekigahara on the night of 20 October 1600 in rain.
shots.accept: Two camps clearly separated left (East) and right (West); rain and night.
shots.caption: Rain falls on the Mino plain. Across the valley, the Western army's fires burn as far as you can see.

shots.subject: Kobayakawa's camp on Matsuo hill
shots.prompt:
A forested hill above the valley at night (Matsuo hill). In a small camp
among the trees, a young lord in a plain dark helmet (Kobayakawa Hideaki)
stands at the edge looking down at both armies' fires, his face uncertain.
His ochre-yellow banners with a black crest hang wet and limp. Messengers
wait behind him. Rain and mist.
shots.history: Kobayakawa Hideaki's 15,000 men held Matsuo hill above the battlefield; both sides courted him.
shots.accept: Ochre banners (not navy or crimson); young lord looking down at two sets of fires; mood of indecision.
shots.caption: On Matsuo hill, Kobayakawa Hideaki waits. Both sides have sent him letters.

shots.subject: Dawn at Sekigahara: fog over both lines
shots.prompt:
Dawn in a narrow valley, thick white fog. Shapes of two armies are barely
visible: rows of banners on the left (navy) and on the right (crimson),
standing in wet fields, spear points above the fog. A road and a stream
cross the valley. Grey-blue light, rain just stopped.
shots.history: Morning of 21 October 1600: dense fog until about 8 a.m.
shots.accept: Fog dominant; both sides implied by banner colour; quiet tension.
shots.caption: Sekigahara, dawn. Fog hides the valley. Somewhere in it, the Western army is waiting.

shots.subject: The fog lifts and the armies face each other
shots.prompt:
The same valley as the fog scene, the fog lifting in bands. Now the
armies are clear: Eastern formations with navy banners advancing across wet
fields on the left; Western formations with crimson banners on low hills on
the right; an arquebus volley's smoke drifting. High wide angle so the whole
field reads like the game's battle map.
shots.history: The battle opened when the fog lifted.
shots.accept: Composition reads left = East, right = West; matches the board's layout.
shots.caption: The fog lifts. The first volleys crack across the valley.

shots.subject: Kobayakawa hesitates as the battle rages
shots.prompt:
Close view on Matsuo hill in daylight, smoke from the battle rising below.
Kobayakawa Hideaki (young, plain dark helmet) grips his war fan, staring
down at the fighting; his generals argue at his side; ochre banners behind
them. Gunsmoke drifts up the slope.
shots.history: Kobayakawa delayed until midday before committing.
shots.accept: Indecision readable in pose; ochre banners; battle implied below.
shots.caption: Kobayakawa watches the battle and does not move.

shots.subject: Kobayakawa's army charges down the hill
shots.prompt:
A dramatic slope view: thousands of Kobayakawa troops with ochre banners
pour down a forested hill into the valley battle, spears levelled, horsemen
leading. The direction of the charge is toward the viewer's lower right.
Gunsmoke and dust, mid-day light through cloud.
shots.history: Used for whichever side he joins; the caption and an on-screen arrow say which side he attacks.
shots.accept: Charge clearly downhill; ochre banners only (no navy or crimson on his men).
shots.caption: Kobayakawa's banners move. His army pours down the hill.

shots.subject: A formation breaks: a falling banner
shots.prompt:
Close, low-angle view in a muddy battlefield: a torn banner on a broken pole
falling toward the mud; behind it, blurred soldiers turning to flee through
smoke. The banner fabric is plain neutral grey so the game can recolour it
for either side. Rain, grim mood, no gore.
shots.history: Reusable for any routed formation; the game tints the banner by side.
shots.accept: Banner is plain grey and central; fleeing silhouettes; no blood.

shots.subject: A camp is taken: a banner raised over it
shots.prompt:
A captured field camp of torn white curtain walls on a low rise; a soldier
plants a tall banner at the centre while others cheer around overturned
stools and a fallen drum. The banner fabric is plain neutral grey so the game
can recolour it for either side. Smoke, late-day light.
shots.history: Reusable for East or West camp captures; the game tints the banner.
shots.accept: Raised banner is the focal point and plain grey; camp clearly overrun.

shots.subject: The Western council at Ōgaki
shots.prompt:
Interior of Ōgaki Castle at night: Ishida Mitsunari (white feather plume on
his helmet, stern, clean-shaven) leans over a map on a low table, pointing.
Around him Western generals; one in a white hood covering his face (Ōtani
Yoshitsugu) listens. Crimson banners on the walls, a single lamp, rain at the
window.
shots.history: Ishida made Ōgaki his headquarters before the battle. Used each chapter for the Western council scene.
shots.accept: Ishida and Ōtani recognizable from the portrait sheet; crimson; no readable map text.
shots.caption: At Ōgaki, Ishida's council plans its next move.

shots.subject: Famine threatens the districts
shots.prompt: A village granary standing empty; thin farmers queue with empty baskets; a samurai official counts the last rice bales; grey autumn light, bare fields.
shots.history: Replaces the shared placeholder used for all five crises in v0.3.1.
shots.accept: Clear at a glance which crisis it is; no gore; no text.
shots.caption: Famine threatens the districts.

shots.prompt:

attached portrait sheet: 3/4 view facing slightly left, detailed pixel-art
armour and helmet, plain near-black background (#0b0a08), soft warm key light
from the left. Young Western general (about 28), handsome, confident; black lacquered armour with crimson lacing; helmet with a distinctive gold crest; clean-shaven. Square 1024x1024. No text.
shots.history: Commander of the largest Western force; currently shown with Ishida's portrait in battle.
shots.accept: Matches the existing eight portraits in framing, scale, lighting and pixel texture.
